To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cannabidiol regulates the one-carbon cycle and methionin levels in Dictyoselium and in mouse models of epilepsy.

1) CBD regulates the one‐carbon metabolism and methionine homeostasis in Dictyosteliam and in mammalian neurons, 2) CBD increases methionine levels by regulating the activity of the one‐carbon metabolic pathway, and 3) CBD‐mediated methionine homeo­stasis regulates neuronal function in mammalian neurons.
cannabidiol regulates the one-carbon cycle, which is a pathway that is essential for the production of methionine, a precursor of S-adenosylmethionine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new mechanisms of action of cannabidiol.
the development and application of new synthetic organic reactions and methods to solve problems in organic synthesis.

the development of new methods of analysis of the composition and structure of complex organic molecules, with the use of these methods for the study of biological systems, and with the development of novel methods for the synthesis of organic molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cannabidiol is a safe drug with few side effects, and is a good alternative treatment for epilepsy, and that it has been approved in the US and UK for the treatment of epilepsy.
cannabidiol is a non‐toxic, non‐psychoactive, non‐addictive compound, which can be safely used in humans and is well tolerated.
CBD has a significant anti-epileptic effect, and that it does so by a number of different mechanisms, some of which are not yet known.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CBD regulates one carbon metabolism and methionine biosynthesis in a manner that could explain the observed clinical efficacy in patients.
we have discovered a new mechanism of action for CBD that is conserved in both the simple model organism Dictyostelium discoideum (Dd) and in mammalian cells.
we have discovered a novel mechanism of action of CBD that is mediated by the regulation of the one-carbon cycle and methionionine levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cannabidiol regulates the methionine cycle and the one carbon cycle in a manner that may be relevant in the context of epilepsy.
cannabidiol is not a panacea for every seizure condition.
the mechanism of action of cannabidiol is not a single, simple pathway.
